subject: Elastic fallback & burst scheduling for LumiCorp Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Huang <daniel.huang@lumicorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Elastic fallback & burst scheduling for LumiCorp Dedicated deployment

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — wanted to capture a practical sizing + burst/fallback proposal so you and procurement have something concrete to review. High level: LumiCorp reserves a baseline Dedicated pool for production and gets an elastic shoulder + ephemeral burst layer that can be used during marketing ramps or nightly batch spikes. Key points below.

Baseline (reserved):
- 16x H100 equivalent (primary production pool)
- Always-on capacity, committed monthly

Shoulder pool (soft reserve):
- 8x GPUs that can be warmed quickly for predictable campaign windows
- First 30 days: complimentary (onboarding credit)

Burst / ephemeral layer:
- Up to 12x preemptible GPUs (H100 or A100 depending on region) for short-lived surges
- Autoscale policy: target linear ramp to full burst within 90s for small increases; 5–10 minute window for sustained >2x baseline traffic
- Fallback behavior: when ephemeral capacity is exhausted, we route to a quantized model variant (r-instruct-quant-v1) or degrade concurrency per-session to preserve latency SLOs

Operational guardrails / SLOs:
- Scale-up SLO: 90s median under synthetic test (integrated with warm KV cache)
- Cold-start avoidance: we keep a tiny prewarmed pool per region to reduce tail latencies
- Cost controls: burst uses discounted spot/preemptible pricing; shoulder pool billed at reserved rate after trial period

Next steps for us:
- I attached a capacity matrix with recommended headroom windows and estimated monthly cost delta (lumicorp_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx).
- Can you share the projected peak QPS curve for the February campaign and the procurement contact who will review T&Cs?

If that looks sensible I can loop in Ben (runtime sizing) and Monica (commercial/commitments) — would love to book a 30-min alignment this week.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Daniel / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for joining the 3pm sync. Summary of commitments from our side and answers to your questions:

1) Pricing & commercials
- Burst (preemptible H100): discounted spot rate at $2.10/GPU-hour (estimate) — final pricing in the MOU.
- Shoulder pool after 30-day credit: billed at reserved slab rate (applies if shoulder is used >30 days cumulatively).
- We will provide a 30-day free shoulder pool trial for onboarding (no charge, limited to the initial production region).

2) Scale/ramp SLOs
- P50 scale-up: ~60s (observed in our warm-KV synthetic tests).
- P95 scale-up: ~180s for 1->3x spike scenarios when colding is required; with prewarmed shoulder this drops to ~110s.
- We will commit to operational runbooks and a warm buffer to keep tail latencies reasonable.

3) Security & compliance
- Ephemeral/preemptible instances will run within your VPC and use your KMS keys; audit logs will be retained for 90 days as requested.

4) Guardrails and cost controls
- Recommended monthly cap on burst hours: start with 600 GPU-hours/month (flexible) to protect against runaway spend; LumiCorp can increase after observing traffic patterns.
- Automatic alerts and hard spend limits can be configured on the Console per-route.

Next steps:
- I attached the capacity matrix and a draft MOU (Lumi_Dedicated_MOU_v1.pdf).
- I’ll send a HubSpot deal record with the official SKU pricing and open a DocuSign for MOU approval: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543 and https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC123456789

Let me know if you want us to scope a 1-week load test with an extended shoulder pool to validate P95 numbers — happy to put that in the MOU.

Best,
Karthik
